subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: PVA and epoxy resin are both types of:
questions.explain: PVA and epoxy resin are adhesives used to bond materials, with epoxy being a strong two-part adhesive.

questions.q: Brass is best described as:
options: An alloy of copper and zinc
A ferrous metal that rusts easily
questions.explain: Brass is an alloy made by combining copper and zinc, giving it good corrosion resistance and machinability.

questions.q: In the 6 Rs of sustainability, 'Refuse' means to:
options: Decline to buy or use something you do not really need
Recycle the material into something new
questions.explain: Refuse means choosing not to buy or use products or materials that are unnecessary or wasteful in the first place.

questions.q: A major social impact of factory automation on a community can be:
questions.explain: Replacing workers with machines can reduce employment, affecting workers and the surrounding community.

questions.q: 'Carbon footprint' of a product refers to:
options: The amount of greenhouse gases produced over its life
The size of the box it ships in
The number of parts it contains
questions.explain: A carbon footprint measures the total greenhouse gas emissions linked to making, using and disposing of a product.

questions.q: Which of these is a manufactured board rather than a natural timber?
questions.explain: MDF is a manufactured board made from compressed wood fibres and resin, whereas oak, pine and mahogany are natural timbers.

questions.q: Motion that swings back and forth on a pivot, like a pendulum, is called:
questions.explain: Oscillating motion swings back and forth around a fixed pivot point, as a pendulum does.

questions.q: Which type of projection shows an object's faces drawn to scale as separate front, plan and side views?
questions.explain: Orthographic projection presents an object as flat, scaled front, side and plan views, typically used for working drawings.

questions.q: A tolerance on a working drawing specifies:
options: The permitted upper and lower limits a dimension may vary between
The exact colour of the product
How long the product should last
questions.explain: A tolerance defines the acceptable maximum and minimum size limits for a dimension, ensuring parts fit together correctly.

questions.q: A driver gear has 10 teeth and the driven gear has 30 teeth. The gear ratio is:
questions.explain: Gear ratio = driven 30 divided by driver 10 = 3, written 3:1, meaning the driver turns three times for each turn of the driven gear.

questions.q: Batch production is best defined as making:
options: A continuous non-stop flow of product 24 hours a day
A specified quantity of identical products in a group, then switching to another
questions.explain: Batch production makes a set number of identical items in one run, after which the equipment can be changed to produce a different batch.

questions.q: The systems approach to electronics describes the order of blocks as:
questions.explain: A system is modelled as input leading to process leading to output, where a signal is received, acted upon, and then produces an action.

questions.q: Which of these is a non-renewable energy source?
questions.explain: Coal is a finite fossil fuel that cannot be replenished, unlike the renewable sources solar, hydro and wind.

questions.q: Anthropometrics is the study of:
questions.explain: Anthropometrics is the collection and use of human body measurements to design products that fit people correctly.

questions.q: Rotary motion is best described as movement that is:
options: Back and forth in a straight line
Turning in a circle around a central point
In a straight line in one direction
Swinging back and forth on a pivot
questions.explain: Rotary motion is movement in a circle around a central axis, such as a wheel or gear turning.

questions.q: An Arduino is best described as:
options: A programmable microcontroller board for controlling inputs and outputs
questions.explain: An Arduino is a programmable microcontroller board used to read sensors and control outputs in projects.

questions.q: Applying a finish such as varnish or paint to a product is done primarily to:
options: Protect the surface and improve appearance
questions.explain: Finishes protect a material from moisture, wear or corrosion and can enhance the product's appearance.

questions.q: An exploded diagram is used to show:
options: How parts fit together by separating them along their assembly lines
questions.explain: An exploded diagram pulls the components apart along their lines of assembly to show how they fit together.

questions.q: A driver pulley of 100 mm diameter drives a 50 mm pulley. The smaller pulley will turn:
options: At the same speed as the driver
questions.explain: A smaller driven pulley rotates faster than a larger driver pulley, increasing output speed.

questions.q: In a third-class lever, such as tweezers, the effort is positioned:
options: Between the fulcrum and the load
questions.explain: A third-class lever has the effort applied between the fulcrum and the load, as with tweezers or a fishing rod.

questions.q: In a pulley system, adding more pulleys (more supporting ropes) generally:
options: Reduces the effort needed to lift the load
Increases the effort needed to lift the load
questions.explain: More supporting rope sections share the load, so less effort is needed to lift it, though the rope must be pulled further.

questions.q: A relay is useful in a circuit because it allows:
options: Charge to be stored long term
A small control current to switch a larger separate circuit
questions.explain: A relay is an electromagnetic switch letting a small current control a much larger or separate circuit safely.
